checks.name: Contract
checks.reason: This check is obsolete as written. It asks that marking an item ready with no contract file fails CI. During this item that semantics was found to be wrong: closing BOOT-001 makes 35 R0 items dependency-clear, and under the old rule every one of them became a ready-item-without-a-contract, so the checker failed the moment the first epic unblocked. Readiness now requires a contract, and unspecified items are held out of the ready set and listed under 'Unblocked but unspecified' instead. The invariant that replaced it — an item marked done without gate evidence must fail — is covered by selftest case 6 and passes. The verification table is not amended here because an implementer may not edit the checks judging its own work; BOOT-001's contract needs a follow-up amendment by someone else.

extra_checks.name: Self-test leaves the working tree unchanged

notes: No independent review took place. GATE-IDENTITY is open, so no reviewer identity exists that is distinct from the implementer, and the doctrine's producer/certifier split is therefore only partially satisfied: the machine gate ran, the human review did not. This is recorded rather than papered over with a fabricated reviewer count. A scope correction was made inside the lease: plan/check.py's readiness semantics changed as described in the Contract check above, and plan/README.md was updated to match. plan/selftest.py is new and is the mechanism behind the three drift checks.
